$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the Appearance section's theme, background, density, pane and focus ring rows (cx-d5b5d). scripts/cmux-next/gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants from it; its docstring is the row format (tabs.json's $comment repeats it, plus choices_from and "swift_case": null). Lists: SettingsSchema.all concatenates them, so rows keep the export's order; schemas/settings/settings-schema.json must not change when rows move here.

rows.note: Reserved for the optional Neko icon family; neko resolves to the default artwork until a reviewed set ships.

help.text: The icon drawings used by cmux.

rows.page_hidden: reserved until the Neko artwork passes light/dark 1x/2x review

rows.note: cmux's terminal theme: a Ghostty theme name or a light/dark pair; unset is the Ghostty config's theme.

help.text: Colors for terminals. A space, workspace or terminal theme overrides it.

summary.text: Colors for terminals, and cmux unless App Theme is set

rows.note: The theme of cmux's own surfaces; followTerminal (the default) uses the terminal theme.

help.text: Colors for the window, sidebar, tabs and pages. Terminals use Terminal Theme.

summary.text: Colors for the window, sidebar, tabs and pages

help.text: Your color changes to a theme, such as "Rose Pine/background": "#1f1d2e".

rows.name: favorites

help.text: Themes starred in a theme picker. The picker lists them first.

rows.palette_hidden: a theme picker's stars edit it: a list of theme names

rows.name: rotation
rows.note: When launch turns appearance.theme to the next starred theme.

help.text: Switches the terminal theme to the next starred one. Needs two starred themes.

summary.text: Change to the next starred theme

choices.note: The first launch of each day.

rows.note: Art Color (art) is no ThemeAccent: the accent takes the hue of the art a window shows (AccentSetting.artID).

help.text: The color of selection, focus and the Send button.

summary.text: Color of selection and focus

rows.note: Off by default: accent is today's rule (the accent's tint when appearance.accent or the theme names one). neutral keeps the gray card whatever the accent (ThemeInput.selection).

help.text: Accent tints the selected row and tab with the accent. Neutral keeps them gray.

summary.text: Color of the selected row and tab

help.text: A theme file in ~/.config/cmux/themes, such as "tokyo" for tokyo.json.

summary.text: A look from ~/.config/cmux/themes

help.text: Settings you changed while a theme file sets them. Your value applies over the file's; resetting the row returns to the file's. Choosing another theme file clears the list.

rows.palette_hidden: a Settings change to a row the theme file sets edits it: a list of setting keys
rows.page_hidden: bookkeeping of the rows changed over the theme file; each row's note says so

help.text: The color of selected text everywhere. Unset uses the terminal theme's.

summary.text: Color of selected text

rows.name: customizeDoctorNotice
rows.note: The app's quiet notice (a toast) at launch and when customization changes, naming a file or layer that changes the person's setup (`cmux customize doctor --announce`, cmux-customize library/doctor.rs). Informational: it changes nothing. Off: no toast; Settings' doctor card and the CLI still list findings. Leo 2026-11-19: "if there's errant files etc that affect customizations it should be able to automatically tell the user and inform them".

summary.text: Tell me when a file or layer changes my setup

rows.note: Legacy: the bundled paintings (BackdropArt) follow None; appearance.background wins when both are set.

help.text: A painting behind the window. Lower Opacity to see it.

summary.text: Painting behind the window

rows.page_hidden: legacy: the wallpaper card's appearance.background replaces it; the key still loads

rows.note: None and Shuffle Paintings, then the bundled art by collection and Desktop Wallpaper (BackdropSelectionSetting.catalogChoices).

help.text: A painting, your wallpaper or a macOS wallpaper behind the window.

summary.text: Image behind your terminals

choices.note: Light and dark: the pictures in appearance.backgroundLight and appearance.backgroundDark, per window appearance.
Time of day: the pictures in appearance.backgroundSchedule, by clock time or sun event.

help.text: How often a shuffled background changes.

summary.text: How often Shuffle changes the picture

rows.name: light
rows.note: The picture of Background's Light and Dark (appearance) in the light appearance: any fixed background id (art, desktop, system:, file:). Unset: the dark side's picture.

help.text: Unset, it shows the dark picture.

rows.name: dark
rows.note: The picture of Background's Light and Dark (appearance) in the dark appearance: any fixed background id. Unset: the light side's picture.

help.text: Unset, it shows the light picture.

rows.name: schedule
rows.note: Background's Time of Day (schedule): when -> fixed background id. When is HH:MM (24 h, local) or sunrise | sunset | dawn | dusk | noon with an optional offset (sunset-30m, sunrise+1h). Now's picture is the latest entry at or before now (before the first: yesterday's last); a sun event that does not happen today is skipped (BackdropTimeOfDay).

help.text: A time (07:00) or sun event (sunset-30m) for each picture.

rows.name: dynamic
rows.note: How a dynamic macOS wallpaper (system: .madesktop or .heic) changes: appearance shows its light or dark frame; time follows the sun (solar metadata), the clock (h24), or for a light/dark-only or not downloaded picture the sun above or below -6 degrees.

help.text: Follow light and dark, or change with the sun through the day.

summary.text: Follow light and dark, or the sun

rows.name: location
rows.note: LAT,LON in degrees for sun events and solar frames; unset: the system time zone's coordinates from /usr/share/zoneinfo/zone.tab (no location permission).

help.text: Latitude,longitude for sunrise and sunset, such as 37.77,-122.42. Unset: your time zone.

rows.name: memory
rows.note: What Background's modes last showed, so switching modes never loses one (Leo, 2026-11-19: "it lost the folder ... i couldn't get back into it"): rotate is Rotate's last shuffle (daily or folder:<path>), folder the last folder it shuffled, off the picture Off last showed (none for No Wallpaper). The Settings page's Background card writes it when the background moves to another mode and reads it back in a new page or after a restart; the app's engine never reads it.

help.text: The folder and picture each background mode last showed, so switching back restores them.

rows.name: placement
rows.note: Where each picture lies in its window or pane (Leo, 2026-11-22: "we also want people to be able to reposition the images easily"): picture id (the id the background shows, a listed painting, file:, system: or a folder's file:) to a placement text, the mode (fill, fit, center or stretch), then optionally the anchor X Y (0 to 1 from the top-left, like CSS object-position) and a zoom (1 to 4). Unset, or a picture with no entry, is today's centered fill. Adjust Background… and the Settings page's Background preview write it; cmux-config backdrop_placement is the math the app mirrors.

help.text: Picture ID to fill, fit, center or stretch, with optional X Y anchor and zoom.

rows.name: recents
rows.note: The backgrounds shown before, newest first (Leo, 2026-11-22: "it was cumbersome back then to switch back"): each an appearance.background value (a rotating folder, daily, desktop, a picture or a mode), at most 8, each once. The daemon's settings write (cmux-config) puts the replaced value first whenever appearance.background changes, from every surface; Switch to Previous Background, Recent Backgrounds…, cmux wallpaper back|recent and the Settings page's Recent strip read it.

help.text: The backgrounds shown before, newest first, so one click goes back.
Display ID to daily, folder:<path>, desktop, a background or none.
Display ID to 15m, hourly or daily. Others use the global rotation.
One background behind the window, or a copy in each pane.

summary.text: One background or one per pane

help.text: The plain theme color, without paintings, wallpapers or glass.
Calm while agents are idle; a soft glow in the machine's color when an agent needs you.

rows.note: Web pages only: on sends glassLevels "previous" with the web theme (WebTheme), data-glass-levels="previous" on <html>, and webviews ui/glass/glass.css (PREVIOUS GLASS) restores the glass numbers from before the one glass system (design/glass-system.md, cmux#48174). Off (default) draws the one glass system.

help.text: Draws menus, popovers, the composer and cards with the glass from before November 2026.
Applies Hue and Saturation to the window's tint. Off, they have no effect.

rows.note: Taste prototype (Taste Board #15): the Settings page draws a small Beta chip beside the title of each experimental row (the Experimental category, labs.* keys, rows tagged labs or experimental) and beside the Experimental sidebar entry (webviews/src/pages/settings/betaChips.ts). Off by default: the page is unchanged.

help.text: Marks experimental settings with a Beta chip.
Draws the knobs of the switches and sliders in Settings as glass.
How much of the theme color covers the material behind the window.

summary.text: Theme color over the backdrop

help.text: Unset, the window follows Ghostty's background-opacity and background-blur.

summary.text: Clear Glass shows the desktop through the wallpaper

help.text: How much windows behind the front one are tinted. 0 keeps them the same.
The glass takes the colors of your desktop picture.
Treats the wallpaper as a light source: glass edges facing its brightest part catch its color, the composer glows with it, and the glass leans toward its hue.
The most frames per second a live wallpaper draws. A wallpaper may ask for fewer; it stops drawing when the window is hidden, idle or on Low Power Mode.

rows.note: Ghostty's background-cells-opacity and background-cells-neutral-fade (ghostty-next), loaded with source cmux-next in GhosttyRuntime.finalizeConfig (GhosttyRuntimeSurfacePolicy.cellBackgroundLines). opaque loads nothing.

help.text: How program-painted cell backgrounds (a TUI's message band, status line) draw over a translucent window or wallpaper: opaque (default), at the window's opacity (window), fading near-background greys to a tint (tint), or both (tintWindow).

rows.name: glassTransparency

help.text: How much of the desktop or wallpaper shows through the glass.

rows.page_hidden: duplicates appearance.backgroundOpacity; the key still loads

help.text: Shift the tint color around the hue wheel.
Increase or reduce the tint color intensity.
Row height, padding, corners, icons and text size together.

rows.palette_hidden: the Density card and the palette's density rows pick it
the Density card edits them: a list of density objects

help.text: Zoom for chat, Settings and other app pages.
Text size of the sidebar, tabs, menus and chat. Terminals have their own size.

rows.note: How cmux's text draws, in the CSS model (-webkit-font-smoothing), native and web. Native: AppleFontSmoothing in the app's domain, written at launch and on each change for the next launch (ProcessFontSmoothing). Web: the web theme's data-cmux-font-smoothing, live (WebTheme). Chrome text cmux draws itself (ChromeLabel, ChromeTextLayer: the sidebar, tabs) follows live too (ProcessFontSmoothing.chrome). Ghostty's font-thicken is not affected.

help.text: How text draws. Some text changes after cmux restarts; terminals keep their own.

rows.note: The font family of cmux's interface, any installed family (Leo, 2026-11-08: "there's no whole app font change thing"). Unset is the system font. Every web page (chat, Settings, palette) takes it as --font-ui live through the web theme (WebTheme.appFontStack, a <style id=cmux-app-font> rule under inline styles, so a chat font set on Chat still wins there). Native chrome text (CheckedFont.system) takes it too while experiments.appFontChrome is on. Terminals keep terminal.fontFamily. Validation domain:ui_font_family: any family name, the owner checks the shape only.

help.text: The font of cmux's interface: chat, Settings and every page. Terminals keep their own.
Text size of tabs, the sidebar and other controls. Terminal text has its own size.

summary.text: Text size of tabs, sidebar and controls

rows.page_hidden: opt-in: the Debug Settings toggle chrome.interfaceSize turns it on, until it is promoted

help.text: None removes every border, hairline and separator in the app.

rows.note: Web pages only: off sends data-glass="off" with the web theme (WebTheme), and every web glass surface draws the solid look of Reduce Transparency (webviews ui/glass/glass.css). Scroll fades stay; native surfaces keep their material. Off by default: CMUX-653, Lawrence decided it at standup 2026-11-19.

help.text: Off draws the composer, menus, popovers and cards as solid surfaces with a plain border.
How the focused pane stands out.

summary.text: How the focused pane stands out

help.text: How other panes' tabs look subtler when Focused Pane marks tabs.

summary.text: How tabs in other panes tone down

rows.note: The window's look; its choices and their titles are schemas/settings/chrome-styles.json (ChromeStyleSetting+Choices.swift).

help.text: Whether panes sit in one rounded card, and where lines are drawn.

summary.text: Card, lines and sidebar background

rows.note: One colour (the default: no shade; the sidebar's edge line, the split panes' lines, the tab row's divider and the selected tab's pill separate) or a subtle tone (half the flush corner's frame shade, scaled by appearance.titleAreaContrast; the selected tab is a folder tab in the content's glass). Only the default flush-corner frame follows it; a picked chrome style keeps its own shade. Leo 2026-11-12: the default is mono-ish as Lawrence wants, with the divider kept across most panes; a refined subtle tone is the option.

help.text: The title bar, tab bar and sidebar in the content's color, or shaded apart.

summary.text: One color or a subtle tone for the title area

rows.note: Scales the chrome's shade around the content card (Metrics.titleAreaShadeScale): Subtle Tone's share of the flush corner's frame, or a picked chrome style's own shade; 2 under Subtle Tone is the older two-tone shade. Leo 2026-11-11: the title area's contrast may be too intense for some people, so it needs to be adjustable.

help.text: How much darker the title bar, tab bar and sidebar are. 1 is the default.

summary.text: How much the title and tab bar stand apart

rows.note: A toggle under any chrome style and any theme: the sidebar and the tab bar in tone A, the content panes (terminal, agent pane, New Tab page, Home) in tone B, the accent fitted to both. Off (the default), From Theme (auto) or a curated pairing; the colors and the pairing table are Rust (cmux-config theme_file::two_tone; the Swift TwoTone mirrors it, checked against the Rust fixture TwoToneTests has Rust write at test time). An explicit appearance.surfaces.<surface>.color wins. Leo 2026-11-19: the two-tone is just one of the toggles you can have; what would actually look good and not eyesore-ish.

help.text: The sidebar and tab bar in one tone, the panes in another. Works with every window style and theme.

summary.text: A second tone for the sidebar and tab bar

choices.note: Tone A from the theme's background and accent; the content keeps the theme's own.

rows.note: How the selected tab meets the content card (CornerFlush, CmuxNextDesign). A missing key is the default, flush with no goo, drawn only over the stock chrome (CornerFlush.defaultFits); a set value draws over any chrome, as a Debug Settings pick of chrome.cornerFlush does, which still overrides it in DEV and NIGHTLY. Compact density keeps the pill under every value. Leo 2026-11-13: "lawrence wanted no goo by default"; Leo 2026-11-18: the gooey look is a toggle a theme or a setup can pick. flush-goo also runs the sidebar's selected row into the card on a block appearance.tabShape (CornerFlush.sidebarRowFlows), and tones the frame under One Color too, since goo needs two tones to show (Leo 2026-11-18: "like the \"gooey\" is each tab looking like it's morphing into the visible pane. the two tone thing.").

help.text: How the selected tab meets the content below it: a pill, flush with it, or flowing into it like a drop of water.

summary.text: Pill, flush or goo for the selected tab

rows.note: How blocky the tabs of every tab bar and the rows of the sidebar are (TabShape, CmuxNextDesign). block (the default) draws today's tabs and rows unchanged. rounded draws the tabs and the sidebar's row fills as capsules, and the selected tab stays a capsule on its strip under every appearance.cornerFlush, never a folder into the content. The gooey look is not a third shape: it is appearance.cornerFlush flush-goo, which on a block shape also runs the sidebar's selected row into the content card (CornerFlush.sidebarRowFlows). Leo 2026-11-18: "the blockiness of tabs both horizontal the the vertical ones in the sidebar should be customized/customizable too."

help.text: The tabs and the sidebar's rows: blocks with the tab's corner, or rounded capsules.

summary.text: Block or rounded tabs and sidebar rows

help.text: Splits, closes, moves, zooms and column scrolls slide into place.
A new tab grows into its place in the tab bar. Off shows it there at once.
A new workspace row opens in the sidebar. Off shows it there at once.

rows.name: paneSeparation
rows.note: Unset follows the curved main pane (Metrics.defaultPaneSeparation).

help.text: How panes are told apart.

summary.text: How panes are told apart

help.text: One radius for panes, tabs, panels, popovers and cards.
Space between a pane's edge and its tabs. Inner corners use the corner radius minus this.
